---
title: "Derived clusters"
---

Besides the raw answers, the preprocessing step derives a few binary/ternary
**cluster** columns used in the analysis. Each groups respondents by a
combination of answers.

```{python}
# | echo: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent))
from _helpers import bar, load_univariate, suppression_note  # noqa: E402
```

## `q01_clustered` — age

Cluster1: under 40s. Cluster2: 40s and over.

```{python}
# | echo: false
bar(load_univariate("q01_clustered"), "q01_clustered", title="Age cluster")
```

## `q13_clustered` — female ratio

Cluster1: reported ratio ≤ 20%. Cluster2: ≥ 40%. Others: in between.

```{python}
# | echo: false
bar(load_univariate("q13_clustered"), "q13_clustered", title="Female-ratio cluster")
```

## `q01q02_clustered` — young researchers by gender

Cluster1: under 40s and Female. Cluster2: under 40s and Male. Others: the rest.

```{python}
# | echo: false
bar(load_univariate("q01q02_clustered"), "q01q02_clustered", title="Young female / male cluster")
```

## `q13q14_clustered` — ratio and satisfaction

Cluster1: reported ratio < 25% **and** rated it Poor/Very Poor.
Cluster2: ratio > 25% **and** rated it Good/Very Good. Others: the rest.

```{python}
# | echo: false
bar(load_univariate("q13q14_clustered"), "q13q14_clustered", title="Ratio-satisfaction cluster")
```
